name: vapor_pressure
source_description: OPERA / EPA PHYSPROP curated experimental vapour-pressure set, the QSAR-ready endpoint file distributed in OPERA_Data.zip of github.com/kmansouri/OPERA. This is the experimental dataset behind Mansouri et al., J Cheminform (2018) 10:10, doi:10.1186/s13321-018-0263-1.
units_evidence: OPERA README.md line 'VP (Log) in mmHg: Vapor Pressure experimental values between 15 and 30 deg C (majority at 25-20C)'. Cross-checked against VP_2.9_update.csv in the same archive, whose 'unit' column is 'mmHg' for all 3945 rows with values on the same log10 scale. No conversion was applied.
temperature_evidence: Per-record 'VP Temperature' field in VP_QR.sdf. Only rows reading exactly 25 were kept. No temperature conversion was performed: extrapolating a 20 C measurement to 25 C needs an enthalpy of vaporisation that this file does not carry.
experimental_only: VP_QR.sdf is OPERA's experimental endpoint file. Every kept row carries a measured LogVP with a literature citation in 'VP Reference' and a measurement temperature. The file holds no prediction column and no predicted/experimental flag; OPERA's predicted values are distributed separately (OPERA_models.zip, the CompTox dashboard) and none were read here.
smiles_note: OPERA's QSAR-ready structure (desalted, neutralised), re-canonicalised by RDKit with isomericSmiles=True. Stereochemistry is retained as given; the OPERA field is largely stereo-free.

curation_steps.detail: dropped 108 records with blank Tr_1_Tst_0 (all also blank temperature, VP Reference '?')
393 distinct literature references; 0 rows without a named reference (kept: they still carry a documented temperature)
kept only rows whose 'VP Temperature' is exactly 25; dropped 287@20C, 10@30C, 9@23C, 8@22C, 7@24C, 5@27C, 4@21C, 4@26C, 4@29C, 2@15C, 1@31C, 1@19C, 1@28C
0 rows carry a '<', '>' or '~' qualifier in LogVP (none found; the field is a bare float throughout, OPERA resolved censoring upstream)
dropped 0 rows whose LogVP is not a float
dropped 0 rows RDKit could not parse; examples: []

caveats: Only 2368 of the paper's 2711 train/test records are at exactly 25 C. The OPERA VP endpoint mixes 15-30 C (README: 'majority at 25-20C'); the 343 rows at other temperatures were dropped rather than extrapolated, so this file is smaller than the ~2,716 structures the 2018 paper reports for the endpoint.
4 of 2368 SMILES carry any stereo marker. OPERA's QSAR-ready curation strips most stereochemistry, so a corpus overlap check on this task should use a connectivity key, not a stereo-aware one.

6 rows measured a salt or solvate while the structure is the desalted parent (Salt_Solvent_ID non-zero): 2,4-D, Dimethylamine salt (CNC), Monosodium methanearsonate ([Na+]), Dodine (CC(=O)O), Formetanate hydrochloride (Cl), (unnamed) (N(CC)(CC)CC), (unnamed) ([Pr+3]). These are kept, as OPERA kept them, but the label does not belong to the structure written beside it. 2,4-D and its dimethylamine salt share one QSAR-ready structure and their reported values differ by 4.9 log units; the acid fell out on temperature, so the salt's value is the one in this file.

2 rows where RDKit's InChIKey for Canonical_QSARr disagrees with the stored InChI Key_QSARr field, i.e. OPERA's own structure/identifier pair is inconsistent there. Left in place; the structure field was treated as authoritative.

No qualifier column exists in VP_QR.sdf, so censored measurements ('<', '>') cannot be identified from this file. LogVP is a bare float in every row. If PHYSPROP censored any of these upstream, that is invisible here.
